rationale: Write-level collaborator could call issue-tracker, wiki and mirror-sync endpoints that require repo admin; guard changed from reqRepoWriter to reqRepoAdmin.
Stale session token of the prebuilds system user stayed valid after claim; token/session lifecycle flaw, fix blocks API key creation for system user and expires keys.
Any authenticated user could delete another user's memo reaction; same commit also fixes attachments, relations, identity providers, registration. Primary: reaction deletion without ownership check.
Read-only collaborator could push via POST git-receive-pack with service=git-upload-pack, since authorization used the query parameter instead of the actual RPC.

Caller of the rotate endpoint could widen a strict or namespace scoped sealed secret to cluster-wide via template annotations, escaping namespace binding. Partly cryptographic scope semantics, hence low confidence.
Suspended user with an already issued API key could still call AI Bridge proxy endpoints; status check was missing in IsAuthorized. Proxy endpoints not in contract.
Non-admin operator could set admin-only allow_private on own webhook subscription via POST/PATCH; response echoed allow_private true. Contract lists field without restriction.
Pull-mode agent credentials were provisioned with excessive RBAC on control plane, allowing admin-level control of federation. Fix is in CLI-generated RBAC rules; HTTP operation not identifiable.
Disabled or expired users and admins could complete password reset and log in; login/password-reset flow logic.

User with general write access could replace a Process Group adding Restricted components without the extra restricted-component permission; restricted authorization was not checked. Contract excerpt does not describe the operation.
